subject: Acme: follow-up + latency/throughput benchmarks (bump)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme discovery — post-call recap & next steps

Hey Jordan — great to speak today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary:
- Use case: customer support summarization + real-time suggestion widget in web app (high QPS, target 50–100 req/s).
- Primary concerns: p99 latency under load, cost per 1k tokens, and security/compliance (SOC2 + VPC requirement).
- Integration: want to route inference through Dedicated pool in us-west with optional fallbacks to hosted for burst.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) Redwood: provide latency/throughput benchmarks on a 512-token prompt profile and a short SOW draft (attached) — by end of day tomorrow (Marissa).
2) Acme: share a small sample prompt set and expected concurrency profile (Jordan) — by EOD Friday.
3) Both: schedule a short follow-up with Marcus (SE) to review bench results and potential tuning — propose Tue 7/6 or Wed 7/7.

Next steps: I attached a one-page SOW draft to expedite procurement. I will run a quick perf sweep tomorrow and send a short report with p50/p95/p99 numbers and throughput curves. If you prefer a deeper soak test we can schedule Marcus to run it on a dedicated pool.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme-sow-draft-20260701.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme discovery — perf benchmarks attached

Jordan — attaching the perf summary we discussed. High-level notes below and the PDF has raw test output and graphs.

Summary of benchmark (512-token prompt, rw-medium-v1, int8):
- Test: 1-hour steady-state test, synthetic prompt mix supplied by Acme (80% short prompts, 20% long).
- Avg latency (token-stream start to first token out): ~85 ms
- p95 latency: ~110 ms
- p99 latency: ~120 ms
- Steady-state throughput: 75–90 requests/sec on a 4-GPU dedicated pool (with batching enabled, batch size tuned to 8 in these tests)
- Observations: KV cache warmed, batching reduced per-request compute by ~30%, occasional p99 spikes during synthetic long prompt bursts (we can tune batching thresholds to mitigate).

Recommendations:
- For your target of 50–100 req/s, the Dedicated pool configuration we tested is a good fit; Marcus can propose a sizing + autoscale policy.
- If sub-100ms p99 is required, we should run a focused tuning pass: shorter batching windows, narrower max-batch size for low-latency critical routes.

I attached: redwood-acme-benchmarks-20260702.pdf (contains graphs + raw metrics) and linked the perf dashboard. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with Marcus to walk through results next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-acme-benchmarks-20260702.pdf
